## Motivation

External checkpoint/restore orchestrators, such as ones built on CRIU and `cuda-checkpoint`, need three things from the server: a signal that it is safe to capture, one idempotent call to bring it back after the restore, and a way to prepare at startup, before state that cannot be captured (such as a P/D KV transfer transport) exists.

SGLang already has the pieces under `--enable-memory-saver`: `pause_generation`, `release_memory_occupation`, `resume_memory_occupation` and `continue_generation`. This PR sequences them behind three routes, so a prepared server behaves exactly like a server paused with `/pause_generation`. It implements the SGLang side of #44523. The vLLM counterpart is vllm-project/vllm#62570.

## Modifications

| API | Behavior |
| :-- | :-- |
| `POST /checkpoint/prepare?mode=abort\|retract` | Pause generation with `mode`, wait for the scheduler to go idle, then release the KV cache. Returns once started, or 400 with the reason and nothing changed if it cannot prepare now. |
| `GET /checkpoint/status` | 200 once prepared, 503 until then, 500 after a failure. |
| `POST /checkpoint/restore` | Bring the KV cache back and continue generation, after a restore or in place. Safe to repeat. |
| `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` | Prepare before the server is marked Up. |
| `Engine.checkpoint_prepare/restore/state` | The same steps in process. |

- The routes are `ADMIN_OPTIONAL`, like `/pause_generation`.
- Between prepare and restore, the server behaves like a paused one: `/ready` and the `/health` canary report 503, and new requests wait until restore.
- `continue_generation` is refused mid-cycle, since it would schedule requests while the KV cache is released.
- Each DP rank replies with the merged state of its TP ranks, so a failure on any TP rank is reported.
- Pipeline parallelism is not supported yet, and prepare returns 400 with it.

Known gap, not changed here: with `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, `pause_generation(mode="abort")` waits only for the requests of the worker that received it, so a late request from another worker can reach the scheduler after the KV cache is released. `pause_generation` + `release_memory_occupation` has the same race today (#45773).

## Validation

On B200 (nscale), together with the PD transport follow-up: Qwen3-0.6B (TP1) and GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (TP4/EP4) prefill and decode servers started with `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` reported `prepared` on `/checkpoint/status`, were captured, and were restored into new pods. After `/checkpoint/resume` (now `/checkpoint/restore`) they returned the same greedy outputs as a live baseline, refused a later prepare with 400 while still serving, and could each be deleted and restored again while the other kept serving.

+"""Process checkpoint lifecycle of one scheduler.
+
+An external orchestrator (for example ai-dynamo/snapshot) captures the whole
+process once it is prepared, restores it elsewhere or keeps it, and resumes
+it. The scheduler goes running -> preparing -> prepared -> running any number
+of times, or ends in failed. Repeated calls are no-ops.
+
+The tokenizer pauses generation as /pause_generation does before preparing,
+and continues it after resuming, so clients see a paused server in between.
+Prepare waits for the paused scheduler to go idle, then releases the KV cache.
+Weights stay on the GPU. Resume brings the KV cache back.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from typing import Callable, Set
+
+from sglang.srt.constants import GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import (
+    CheckpointReqInput,
+    CheckpointReqOutput,
+    CheckpointReqType,
+    CheckpointState,
+    ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+    ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class SchedulerCheckpointLifecycle:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        enable_memory_saver: bool,
+        offload_tags: Set[str],
+        is_engine_paused: Callable[[], bool],
+        is_fully_idle: Callable[..., bool],
+        release_memory_occupation: Callable[[ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],
+        resume_memory_occupation: Callable[[ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self._enable_memory_saver = enable_memory_saver
+        # Live view of the memory regions released through the admin API.
+        self._offload_tags = offload_tags
+        self._is_engine_paused = is_engine_paused
+        self._is_fully_idle = is_fully_idle
+        self._release_memory_occupation = release_memory_occupation
+        self._resume_memory_occupation = resume_memory_occupation
+        self.state = CheckpointState.RUNNING
+        self._error = ""
+
+    def handle(self, recv_req: CheckpointReqInput) -> CheckpointReqOutput:
+        # STATE reports whether PREPARE would be refused; repeats are no-ops.
+        success, message = True, ""
+        if self.state == CheckpointState.FAILED:
+            success = False
+        elif recv_req.req_type == CheckpointReqType.RESUME:
+            if self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARING:
+                success, message = False, "Cannot resume while preparing"
+            elif self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARED:
+                logger.info("Resuming from a process checkpoint")
+                try:
+                    self._resume_memory_occupation(
+                        ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=[GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE])
+                    )
+                except Exception as e:
+                    self.state = CheckpointState.FAILED
+                    self._error = f"Failed to resume from the checkpoint: {e}"
+                    logger.exception(self._error)
+                else:
+                    self.state = CheckpointState.RUNNING
+        elif self.state == CheckpointState.RUNNING:
+            if not self._enable_memory_saver:
+                success = False
+                message = "Preparing for a checkpoint requires --enable-memory-saver"
+            elif self._offload_tags:
+                success = False
+                message = f"Memory is already released: {sorted(self._offload_tags)}"
+            elif self._is_engine_paused() and not self._is_drained():
+                # A paused scheduler no longer advances its grammar, KV transfer
+                # or HiCache queues, so a retract pause not idle now never is.
+                success = False
+                message = (
+                    "Cannot drain a retract pause while requests wait on grammar, "
+                    "KV transfer or HiCache work; use mode=abort"
+                )
+            elif recv_req.req_type == CheckpointReqType.PREPARE:
+                logger.info("Preparing for a process checkpoint")
+                self.state = CheckpointState.PREPARING
+                self.check_pending()

The trigger for GPU snapshot should probably be a wrapper like https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/43965 instead. This PR (and the follow-ups) are mainly focused on how to prepare the engine for a checkpoint and restoring those resources afterwards.

In the future we can allow configuration of what to do with weights/KV cache. For instance, whether we use the WCD's VMM backend to get rid of weights from the checkpoint, or have the weights offloaded, or keep the weights in GPU memory (which we do for now). And similarly for the KV cache as well.

+running -> preparing -> prepared -> running any number of times, or ends in
+failed. Repeated calls are no-ops.
+
+The tokenizer pauses generation as /pause_generation does before preparing,
+and continues it after resuming, so clients see a paused server in between.
+Prepare waits for the paused scheduler to go idle, then releases the KV cache.
+Weights stay on the GPU. Resume brings the KV cache back.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from typing import Any, Callable, List, Set
+
+from sglang.srt.constants import GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import (
+    CheckpointReqInput,
+    CheckpointReqOutput,
+    CheckpointReqType,
+    CheckpointState,
+    ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+    ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class SchedulerCheckpointManager:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        enable_memory_saver: bool,
+        pp_size: int,
+        offload_tags: Set[str],
+        is_engine_paused: Callable[[], bool],
+        is_fully_idle: Callable[..., bool],
+        release_memory_occupation: Callable[[ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],
+        resume_memory_occupation: Callable[[ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],
+        all_gather_object: Callable[[Any], List[Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        self._enable_memory_saver = enable_memory_saver
+        self._pp_size = pp_size
+        # Live view of the memory regions released through the admin API.
+        self._offload_tags = offload_tags
+        self._is_engine_paused = is_engine_paused
+        self._is_fully_idle = is_fully_idle
+        self._release_memory_occupation = release_memory_occupation
+        self._resume_memory_occupation = resume_memory_occupation
+        # Over the TP ranks of this DP rank.
+        self._all_gather_object = all_gather_object
+        self.state = CheckpointState.RUNNING
+        self._error = ""
+
+    def handle(self, recv_req: CheckpointReqInput) -> CheckpointReqOutput:
+        # STATE reports whether PREPARE would be refused. Repeats are no-ops.
+        success, message = True, ""
+        if self.state == CheckpointState.FAILED:
+            success = False
+        elif recv_req.req_type == CheckpointReqType.RESUME:
+            if self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARING:
+                success, message = False, "Cannot resume while preparing"
+            elif self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARED:
+                logger.info("Resuming from a process checkpoint")
+                try:
+                    self._resume_memory_occupation(
+                        ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=[GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE])
+                    )
+                except Exception as e:
+                    self.state = CheckpointState.FAILED
+                    self._error = f"Failed to resume from the checkpoint: {e}"
+                    logger.exception(self._error)
+                else:
+                    self.state = CheckpointState.RUNNING
+        elif self.state == CheckpointState.RUNNING:
+            if not self._enable_memory_saver:
+                success = False
+                message = "Preparing for a checkpoint requires --enable-memory-saver"
+            elif self._pp_size > 1:
+                success = False
+                message = (
+                    "Preparing for a checkpoint does not support pipeline parallelism"
+                )
+            elif self._offload_tags:
+                success = False
+                message = f"Memory is already released: {sorted(self._offload_tags)}"
+            elif self._is_engine_paused() and not self._is_drained():
+                # A paused scheduler no longer advances its grammar, KV transfer
+                # or HiCache queues, so a retract pause not idle now never is.
+                success = False
+                message = (
+                    "Cannot drain a retract pause while requests wait on grammar, "
+                    "KV transfer or HiCache work. Use mode=abort"
+                )
+            elif recv_req.req_type == CheckpointReqType.PREPARE:
+                logger.info("Preparing for a process checkpoint")
+                self.state = CheckpointState.PREPARING
+                self.check_pending()
+        out = CheckpointReqOutput(
+            success=success, message=message or self._error, state=self.state
+        )
+        # Only the first TP rank replies to the tokenizer, so it reports them all.
+        # Every TP rank handles this request in the same scheduler iteration.
+        return CheckpointReqOutput.merge(self._all_gather_object(out))
+
+    def check_pending(self) -> None:
+        """Finish preparing once the drain is complete."""
+        if self.state != CheckpointState.PREPARING or not self._is_drained():
+            return
+        try:
+            self._release_memory_occupation(
+                ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=[GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE])
+            )

detail.body:
## Motivation

External checkpoint/restore orchestrators, such as ones built on CRIU and `cuda-checkpoint`, need three things from the server: a signal that it is safe to capture, one idempotent call to bring it back after the restore, and a way to prepare at startup, before state that cannot be captured (such as a P/D KV transfer transport) exists.

SGLang already has the pieces under `--enable-memory-saver`: `pause_generation`, `release_memory_occupation`, `resume_memory_occupation` and `continue_generation`. This PR sequences them behind three routes, so a prepared server behaves exactly like a server paused with `/pause_generation`. It implements the SGLang side of #44523. The vLLM counterpart is vllm-project/vllm#62570.

## Modifications

| API | Behavior |
| :-- | :-- |
| `POST /checkpoint/prepare?mode=abort\|retract` | Pause generation with `mode`, wait for the scheduler to go idle, then release the KV cache. Returns once started, or 400 with the reason and nothing changed if it cannot prepare now. |
| `GET /checkpoint/status` | 200 once prepared, 503 until then, 500 after a failure. |
| `POST /checkpoint/restore` | Bring the KV cache back and continue generation, after a restore or in place. Safe to repeat. |
| `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` | Prepare before the server is marked Up. |
| `Engine.checkpoint_prepare/restore/state` | The same steps in process. |

- The routes are `ADMIN_OPTIONAL`, like `/pause_generation`.
- Between prepare and restore, the server behaves like a paused one: `/ready` and the `/health` canary report 503, and new requests wait until restore.
- `continue_generation` is refused mid-cycle, since it would schedule requests while the KV cache is released.
- Each DP rank replies with the merged state of its TP ranks, so a failure on any TP rank is reported.
- Pipeline parallelism is not supported yet, and prepare returns 400 with it.

Known gap, not changed here: with `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, `pause_generation(mode="abort")` waits only for the requests of the worker that received it, so a late request from another worker can reach the scheduler after the KV cache is released. `pause_generation` + `release_memory_occupation` has the same race today (#45773).

## Validation

On B200 (nscale), together with the PD transport follow-up: Qwen3-0.6B (TP1) and GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (TP4/EP4) prefill and decode servers started with `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` reported `prepared` on `/checkpoint/status`, were captured, and were restored into new pods. After `/checkpoint/resume` (now `/checkpoint/restore`) they returned the same greedy outputs as a live baseline, refused a later prepare with 400 while still serving, and could each be deleted and restored again while the other kept serving.

+"""Process checkpoint state of one scheduler.
+
+An external orchestrator captures the whole process once it is prepared,
+then restores it, in a process started from the capture or in place. The
+scheduler goes running -> preparing -> prepared -> running any number of
+times, or ends in failed. Repeated calls are no-ops.
+
+The tokenizer pauses generation as /pause_generation does before preparing,
+and continues it after restoring, so clients see a paused server in between.
+Prepare waits for the paused scheduler to go idle, then releases the KV cache.
+Weights stay on the GPU. Restore brings the KV cache back.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from typing import Any, Callable, List, Set
+
+from sglang.srt.constants import GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import (
+    CheckpointReqInput,
+    CheckpointReqOutput,
+    CheckpointReqType,
+    CheckpointState,
+    ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+    ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class SchedulerCheckpointManager:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        enable_memory_saver: bool,
+        pp_size: int,
+        offload_tags: Set[str],
+        is_engine_paused: Callable[[], bool],
+        is_fully_idle: Callable[..., bool],
+        release_memory_occupation: Callable[[ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],
+        resume_memory_occupation: Callable[[ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],
+        all_gather_object: Callable[[Any], List[Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        self._enable_memory_saver = enable_memory_saver
+        self._pp_size = pp_size
+        # Live view of the memory regions released through the admin API.
+        self._offload_tags = offload_tags
+        self._is_engine_paused = is_engine_paused
+        self._is_fully_idle = is_fully_idle
+        self._release_memory_occupation = release_memory_occupation
+        self._resume_memory_occupation = resume_memory_occupation
+        # Over the TP ranks of this DP rank.
+        self._all_gather_object = all_gather_object
+        self.state = CheckpointState.RUNNING
+        self._error = ""
+
+    def handle(self, recv_req: CheckpointReqInput) -> CheckpointReqOutput:
+        # STATE reports whether PREPARE would be refused. Repeats are no-ops.
+        success, message = True, ""
+        if self.state == CheckpointState.FAILED:
+            success = False
+        elif recv_req.req_type == CheckpointReqType.RESTORE:
+            if self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARING:
+                success, message = False, "Cannot restore while preparing"
+            elif self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARED:

+import asyncio
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import CheckpointState
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.checkpoint_manager import (
+    SchedulerCheckpointManager,
+)

+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _server(*drained, tp_size=1, release_error=None):
+    """A tokenizer over real scheduler checkpoint managers, `tp_size` per DP
+    rank. `drained` says whether each DP rank goes idle, and the last TP rank
+    of each fails its KV cache release with `release_error`. Pause, continue
+    and the KV cache release are recorded in `calls`."""
+    calls = []
+    engine_paused = [False]
+
+    async def pause_generation(obj):
+        calls.append("pause")
+        # Abort only holds requests in the tokenizer. Retract pauses the scheduler.
+        engine_paused[0] = obj.mode == "retract"
+
+    async def continue_generation(obj):
+        calls.append("continue")
+        engine_paused[0] = False
+
+    def release(fails):
+        def release_memory_occupation(req):
+            if fails and release_error is not None:
+                raise release_error
+            calls.append("release")
+
+        return release_memory_occupation
+
+    # TP ranks of a DP rank handle each request in turn, the first one last,
+    # and see every output gathered so far.
+    gathered = []
+
+    def all_gather_object(out):
+        gathered.append(out)
+        return list(gathered)
+
+    ranks = [
+        SchedulerCheckpointManager(
+            enable_memory_saver=True,
+            pp_size=1,
+            offload_tags=set(),
+            is_engine_paused=lambda: engine_paused[0],
+            is_fully_idle=MagicMock(return_value=idle),
+            release_memory_occupation=release(fails=tp_rank == tp_size - 1),
+            resume_memory_occupation=lambda req: calls.append("resume_kv"),
+            all_gather_object=all_gather_object,
+        )
+        for idle in drained
+        for tp_rank in range(tp_size)
+    ]
+
+    async def checkpoint_communicator(obj):
+        # Only the first TP rank of each DP rank replies.
+        replies = []
+        for dp_rank in range(len(drained)):
+            gathered.clear()
+            tp_ranks = ranks[dp_rank * tp_size : (dp_rank + 1) * tp_size]
+            replies.append([rank.handle(obj) for rank in reversed(tp_ranks)][-1])
+        return replies
+
+    tokenizer = SimpleNamespace(
+        auto_create_handle_loop=lambda: None,
+        checkpoint_lock=asyncio.Lock(),
+        is_pause=False,
+        checkpoint_communicator=checkpoint_communicator,
+        pause_generation=pause_generation,
+        continue_generation=continue_generation,
+    )

+        TokenizerControlMixin._call_checkpoint(tokenizer, req_type)
+    )
+    return tokenizer, ranks, calls
+
+

+    return asyncio.run(TokenizerControlMixin.checkpoint_prepare(tokenizer, mode))
+
+
+def _restore(tokenizer):
+    return asyncio.run(TokenizerControlMixin.checkpoint_restore(tokenizer))
+
+
+class TestCheckpointManager(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_prepare_releases_kv_cache_only_after_pause_and_drain(self):
+        """A request scheduled after the KV cache is released runs without one,
+        so generation is paused first and the release waits for the drain.
+        Orchestrators redeliver prepare, so a repeat is a no-op."""
+        tokenizer, ranks, calls = _server(True, False)
+
+        out = _prepare(tokenizer)
+        self.assertTrue(out.success)
+        self.assertEqual(out.state, CheckpointState.PREPARING)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, ["pause", "release"])
+
+        ranks[1]._is_fully_idle.return_value = True
+        ranks[1].check_pending()
+        out = _prepare(tokenizer)
+        self.assertEqual(out.state, CheckpointState.PREPARED)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, ["pause", "release", "release"])

+        HiCache work, so a busy rank never drains. The refusal must come before
+        any rank releases its KV cache, and the pause must be undone."""
+        tokenizer, ranks, calls = _server(False, True)

+        """Orchestrators redeliver restore. A repeat must not lift a pause a user
+        started after the cycle ended."""
+        tokenizer, ranks, calls = _server(True, True)
+        _prepare(tokenizer)

+        self.assertEqual(_restore(tokenizer).state, CheckpointState.RUNNING)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, ["resume_kv", "resume_kv", "continue"])
+        self.assertEqual(_restore(tokenizer).state, CheckpointState.RUNNING)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, ["resume_kv", "resume_kv", "continue"])
+
+    def test_failed_release_latches(self):
+        """Restoring a half-released server would serve without a KV cache, so a
+        failure stops it for good and generation stays paused."""
+        tokenizer, ranks, calls = _server(True, release_error=RuntimeError("oom"))
+
+        out = _prepare(tokenizer)
+        self.assertEqual(out.state, CheckpointState.FAILED)
+        self.assertIn("oom", out.message)
+        out = _restore(tokenizer)
+        self.assertFalse(out.success)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, ["pause"])
+
+    def test_failure_on_a_tp_rank_that_does_not_reply_is_reported(self):
+        """Only the first TP rank of a DP rank replies to the tokenizer. If
+        another one fails to release its KV cache, the server must not report
+        prepared, or it would be captured with that KV cache."""
+        tokenizer, ranks, calls = _server(
+            True, tp_size=2, release_error=RuntimeError("oom")
+        )
+
+        out = _prepare(tokenizer)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [r.state for r in ranks], [CheckpointState.PREPARED, CheckpointState.FAILED]
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(out.state, CheckpointState.FAILED)
+        self.assertIn("oom", out.message)
+
+

+"""Process checkpoint lifecycle of one scheduler.
+
+An external orchestrator (for example ai-dynamo/snapshot) captures the whole
+process once it is prepared, restores it elsewhere or keeps it, and resumes
+it. The scheduler goes running -> preparing -> prepared -> running any number
+of times, or ends in failed. Repeated calls are no-ops.
+
+The tokenizer pauses generation as /pause_generation does before preparing,
+and continues it after resuming, so clients see a paused server in between.
+Prepare waits for the paused scheduler to go idle, then releases the KV cache.
+Weights stay on the GPU. Resume brings the KV cache back.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from typing import Callable, Set
+
+from sglang.srt.constants import GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import (
+    CheckpointReqInput,
+    CheckpointReqOutput,
+    CheckpointReqType,
+    CheckpointState,
+    ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+    ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class SchedulerCheckpointLifecycle:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        enable_memory_saver: bool,
+        offload_tags: Set[str],
+        is_engine_paused: Callable[[], bool],
+        is_fully_idle: Callable[..., bool],
+        release_memory_occupation: Callable[[ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],
+        resume_memory_occupation: Callable[[ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self._enable_memory_saver = enable_memory_saver
+        # Live view of the memory regions released through the admin API.
+        self._offload_tags = offload_tags
+        self._is_engine_paused = is_engine_paused
+        self._is_fully_idle = is_fully_idle
+        self._release_memory_occupation = release_memory_occupation
+        self._resume_memory_occupation = resume_memory_occupation
+        self.state = CheckpointState.RUNNING
+        self._error = ""
+
+    def handle(self, recv_req: CheckpointReqInput) -> CheckpointReqOutput:
+        # STATE reports whether PREPARE would be refused; repeats are no-ops.
+        success, message = True, ""
+        if self.state == CheckpointState.FAILED:
+            success = False
+        elif recv_req.req_type == CheckpointReqType.RESUME:
+            if self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARING:
+                success, message = False, "Cannot resume while preparing"
+            elif self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARED:
+                logger.info("Resuming from a process checkpoint")
+                try:
+                    self._resume_memory_occupation(
+                        ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=[GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE])
+                    )
+                except Exception as e:
+                    self.state = CheckpointState.FAILED
+                    self._error = f"Failed to resume from the checkpoint: {e}"
+                    logger.exception(self._error)
+                else:
+                    self.state = CheckpointState.RUNNING
+        elif self.state == CheckpointState.RUNNING:
+            if not self._enable_memory_saver:
+                success = False
+                message = "Preparing for a checkpoint requires --enable-memory-saver"
+            elif self._offload_tags:
+                success = False
+                message = f"Memory is already released: {sorted(self._offload_tags)}"
+            elif self._is_engine_paused() and not self._is_drained():
+                # A paused scheduler no longer advances its grammar, KV transfer
+                # or HiCache queues, so a retract pause not idle now never is.
+                success = False
+                message = (
+                    "Cannot drain a retract pause while requests wait on grammar, "

+                )
+            elif recv_req.req_type == CheckpointReqType.PREPARE:
+                logger.info("Preparing for a process checkpoint")

+from typing import Any, Callable, List, Set

+    ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput,

+

+    def __init__(

+        resume_memory_occupation: Callable[[ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput], None],

+        self._pp_size = pp_size
+        # Live view of the memory regions released through the admin API.

+        self.state = CheckpointState.RUNNING
+        self._error = ""
+

+        # STATE reports whether PREPARE would be refused. Repeats are no-ops.
+        success, message = True, ""
+        if self.state == CheckpointState.FAILED:
+            success = False
+        elif recv_req.req_type == CheckpointReqType.RESUME:
+            if self.state == CheckpointState.PREPARING:

+                message = "Preparing for a checkpoint requires --enable-memory-saver"
+            elif self._pp_size > 1:

+                )
+            elif self._offload_tags:
+                success = False

+            elif self._is_engine_paused() and not self._is_drained():

+            )
